problem:
Consider the function $F(x)=|x|$ defined on $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ).$ The Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼\frac{\pi }{2}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{\pi (2n-1)^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)x).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.At $x=0,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)\cdot 0)={{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is 
{{field-2}}
at $x=0,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(0)={{field-3}}.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}={{field-4}}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)\cdot 0)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=0,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(0)=0.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡((2n-1)\cdot 0) \\ 0 & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot 1 \\ -\frac{\pi }{2} & =-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}} & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
